newsitem.title: USA: Chad sees weak sales for next two quarters.
newsitem.headline: Chad sees weak sales for next two quarters.

text.p: Chad Therapeutics In, a provider of oxygen conserving devices and portable oxygen systems, on Tuesday said it expects weak sales to continue through the next two quarters.

Earlier, Chad reported a net profit of $702,000, or $0.07 a share, for its fiscal fourth quarter ended March 31, versus $1.4 million, or $0.13 a share last year. Quarterly sales were $5.07 million, a drop of $94,000 from the year ago quarter.
"These conditions and uncertainties will likely continue to influence quarterly comparisons during the next two quarters," the company said in a statement.
Chad noted, however, that it remains "well-positioned" in its markets with "highly efficient and cost effective products."

The fourth quarter's overall revenues were hurt by sales to national chain accounts that fell by 13 percent from fiscal 1996's fourth quarter. The company cited fewer health care programs converting patients as a reason for the decrease.
Also, sales to national chain accounts and independent dealers were impacted by increased competition and uncertainty about potential cuts in Medicare home oxygen reimbursement.
